newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says patience needed for Middle East peace.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says patience needed for Middle East peace.

text.p: Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak said after talks with Jordan's King Hussein on Tuesday that patience with Israel was needed to overcome difficulties in the Middle East peace process.

"I can't give a fixed time for being patient with the Israeli prime minister knowing the difficulties he is leading. But let us try to help so that he can proceed forward," he told reporters after talks with the Jordanian monarch.

He was responding to a question about a time frame for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has angered Arabs since he took office in May for not carrying out fully a peace accord signed by his predecessor.
Netanyahu has said modifications were needed for security reasons before any Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron, the last West Bank town to be handed over to the Palestinians.
"And as he (Netanyahu) told me several times that he is honouring his commitment, we would like to help him so that he is able to really honour the commitment with his colleagues," Mubarak said.
King Hussein said this approach would "...give us hopefully, sometime soon, cause to rejoice in terms of the surprise that he (Netanyahu) has promised both of us. Let's hope that it comes."
The two leaders, whose countries have peace treaties with Israel, met at this Sinai resort to try to find a new approach to injecting vigour into the stalled Arab-Israeli talks.
They said the peace process might have hit a rough patch lately but it was irreversible and would eventually succeed.
Israel and the PLO in Tel Aviv on Tuesday kept in motion talks on the redeployment despite the absence from the region of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and a U.S. mediator.

U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, ending three weeks of marathon mediation in a bid to nail down details of the long-delayed pullout from the West Bank town, left for Washington and Arafat was in Norway, the first leg of a European tour.
Mubarak and King Hussein urged Europe to join the United States in pushing the process forward.

"The wheel of the peace process has already moved...Nobody will be able to stop this wheel from moving forward. There may be some obstacles every now and then but nobody will be able to put more difficulties on the process," Mubarak said.
Netanyahu said on Tuesday the PLO was delaying a deal on redeployment confident Israel would be blamed. The U.S. said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat alone could not be blamed.
King Hussein agreed with Mubarak that there was no turning back from any peace started with Israel.
"I agree with my brother totally," King Hussein said. "I believe the momentum is there. We are facing a difficult moment but it does not cause us to despair," he said.
Israel's security sources said defence chiefs told Netanyahu that the army needed more than $1 billion because of an increased chance of war with Syria.
"We appeal to the Israeli government not to mention war from time to time as it will be harmful to both sides. It is a three-letter word but its effects are very dangerous," Mubarak said.

The Jordanian monarch said he and Mubarak agreed they saw a role for Europe to complement the U.S. sponsorship "so that the moral weight of the world can be felt in pushing the peace process forward".
The European Union has pressed for a wider role in peace talks but Israel is not convinced that it will be neutral.
